providers.title: Code providers
providers.description: Connect the GitHub App to one or more organizations, then pick in GitHub which repositories get scanned.
providers.github_tagline: GitHub App · reads the code and comments on pull requests
providers.key_note: The App's private key is encrypted on the server. Each scan mints a one-hour token that lives only in memory.
providers.forget_confirm: This removes the key and the connection from this server. The App still exists on GitHub: delete it there if you no longer need it.

pending.gitlab: With a read-only project token, so access is limited to the projects you choose.
pending.bitbucket: With a read-only repository access token.
pending.azure: Through Microsoft Entra ID, the method Microsoft supports since 2025.

repositories.title: Repositories
repositories.description: Repositories granted across every connected organization.
repositories.batch_running: A batch is already running: wait for it or cancel it.
repositories.batch_limit: Up to 100; for more, scan the whole organization.

search.label: Search for a repository
search.partial: Partial results: this account's repository list is still being read from GitHub.

github.pem_too_large: That file is too large to be a .pem key
github.pem_invalid: That file doesn't look like a GitHub App private key (.pem)

open.title: Open the new GitHub App form
open.body: Under your personal account or an organization you administer (enter its name):

name.title: Name and homepage
name.app_name: GitHub App name: anything you like, e.g. (it must be unique on GitHub; add your team's name if it's taken).
name.homepage: Homepage URL: any URL of yours, e.g.

hooks.title: No OAuth or webhooks
hooks.callback: Leave Callback URL empty and "Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation" unchecked.
hooks.setup: Setup URL (optional, brings you back here after installing): and check "Redirect on update".
hooks.webhook: Under Webhook, uncheck "Active": the panel polls pull requests itself, so it doesn't need to be reachable from the internet.

permissions.title: Permissions: only these four
permissions.outro: Nothing under Organization or Account permissions, and no events. The less access the App has, the less damage a leaked key can do.

install_scope.title: Where it can be installed
install_scope.body: Under "Where can this GitHub App be installed?" choose Any account if you'll connect several organizations. Then click Create GitHub App.

key.title: Copy the App ID and generate the private key
key.body: The App ID is at the top, under "About". Scroll down to Private keys and click "Generate a private key": a .pem file downloads.

form.title: 7 · Connect it here
form.description: The panel checks with GitHub that the key belongs to that App before saving anything.
form.admin_only: Only an administrator can connect the GitHub App.
form.env_missing: The server has GITHUB_APP_ID in its environment, but it's missing: {{missing}}.
form.key_note: The key is stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) on the server; it never comes back to the browser or shows up in logs. Afterwards, delete the .pem from your downloads folder.

install.next_connected: You can add another organization and choose its repositories.
install.next_first: Install it on the organizations you need and choose their repositories.
install.step_install: Click Install on GitHub and choose Only select repositories, picking the ones you want to scan.
install.step_detect: Come back and click Find installations, then select the organizations you want to use in this workspace.
install.installed_on: Accounts where the App is installed

permission_warning.excess_body: Review the GitHub App's permissions; installed repositories keep the scope you chose.
permission_warning.missing: Missing permissions: {{permissions}}. Without them, pull requests aren't reviewed.
permission_warning.missing_pending: Missing permissions: {{permissions}} (a permission update is waiting to be accepted on the installation). Without them, pull requests aren't reviewed.

registries.title: Container registries
registries.description: For scanning private images (New scan → Container image). Public images need nothing. Always use a read-only token.
registries.stored_note: Encrypted on the server; it never comes back to the browser or shows up in logs. Saving again for the same registry replaces it.
registries.admin_only: Only an administrator can save registry credentials.
registries.help: What to enter for each registry

docker.token: read-only access token (Account settings → Personal access tokens)

ecr.token: output of aws ecr get-login-password (expires after 12 h)

gar.token: key for a service account with Artifact Registry Reader

registries.private_blocked: Registries on your internal network (private IPs) are blocked so nobody can use the panel to reach internal services. To allow them, start the server with TAMANDUA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_REGISTRIES=1.

kind_hint.api: REST or GraphQL with no interface.
kind_hint.surface: A host you only want to inventory.

list.title: Domains and APIs
list.description: Register HTTPS targets you own and prove ownership with a DNS TXT record. Registering or verifying doesn't start any test.

add.title: Add domain
add.description: Register a domain or API you own so you can pick it as a target.
add.checking: Checking whether it responds over HTTPS…
add.context_placeholder: What does this app do? Stack, authentication, sensitive data it handles…
add.context_note: {{length}}/400 · kept with the asset as a team note; the system doesn't verify it.

verify.title: Domain added
verify.description: Prove ownership with a DNS TXT record before any active testing.
verify.instructions: Add this TXT record at your DNS provider:
verify.no_tests: Verifying ownership doesn't launch any test: it makes the domain an eligible target.
